mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior month's level coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior month's value by at least 0.25 percentage points
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not show statistically significant negative excess returns (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses up, compared to the prior month's close.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 50,000 by at least 20,000 jobs in the current month
failure_condition: Across 24 months of such labor additions, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of non-trigger months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 2% or more in the current month relative to the prior month
regime_hint: Early-cycle soft landing turning into soft landing risk
failure_condition: In 30 such monthly INDPRO declines, the 5-day forward returns are not persistently negative (average excess return ≥ 0, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 0.5% each month indicate deflationary pressure and suppresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < prev_month and INDPRO < prev_month by at least 0.5%
failure_condition: During 8 such co-occurrences, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than baseline (mean excess return ≥ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in goods orders (GDPC1) of more than 10% in a quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening business confidence and tighter credit conditions.
failure_condition: Over 5 such quarters, the 20-day forward returns during contractions are not systematically negative (average excess return ≥ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% indicates a labor market tightening that, when combined with rising inflation proxies, can drive a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.5% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3% over the same period
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, 60-day forward returns do not show statistically significant positive excess returns (mean excess return ≤ 0, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail jobs added (PAYEMS) below -50,000 for a month signals a softening labor market, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < prev_month by at least 50,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: In 12 such monthly drops, the 5-day forward returns are not persistently negative (average excess return ≥ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS path) above 4.5% for 10 consecutive months is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% for 10 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 8 such 10-month high-rate periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (mean excess return ≥ 0, p > 0.05).
